per_channel_states: HANDSHAKE (VALID=1, READY=1 on rising ACLK -> transfer occurs)
fsm_hints.rule: Source MUST NOT wait for READY before asserting VALID. Destination MAY wait for VALID before asserting READY. Once VALID is asserted it must remain asserted until handshake (cannot be retracted).

write_transaction_fsm_master: Drive AWADDR + AW* fields; assert AWVALID.
Drive WDATA[0]+WSTRB+WLAST=0 (or WLAST=1 if single beat); assert WVALID.
Wait for AWREADY and WREADY handshakes (in any order).
Drive remaining beats with WLAST=1 on the final beat.
Wait for BVALID; assert BREADY to accept BRESP.
read_transaction_fsm_master: Drive ARADDR + AR* fields; assert ARVALID.
Slave drives RDATA / RRESP / RLAST and asserts RVALID per beat.
Master asserts RREADY to accept each beat; RLAST=1 on the final beat.

channel_dependency_rules_AXI4_AXI5_write.note: AXI4/AXI5 add an additional slave dependency on AW handshake before BVALID, so slaves take responsibility for hazard checking against subsequent transactions.

fields.anti_deadlock_rule: Inside the slave, VALID for an outgoing channel must not be combinationally dependent on the READY of an incoming channel.
fields.exit_from_reset: Earliest point after reset that a master may drive ARVALID/AWVALID/WVALID HIGH is the rising ACLK edge after ARESETn=HIGH.

default_ready_state_recommendation.AWREADY: Default HIGH recommended (slave must accept any valid address in one cycle).
default_ready_state_recommendation.WREADY: May default HIGH only if slave can always accept write data in one cycle.
default_ready_state_recommendation.BREADY: May default HIGH only if master can always accept a write response in one cycle.
default_ready_state_recommendation.RREADY: May default HIGH only if master can accept read data immediately at start of read.

interleaving.AXI3: Write data with different IDs (via WID) was permitted to be interleaved.
interleaving.AXI4_AXI5: Write data interleaving is deprecated. Write data must be issued in address-channel order.

evidence.quote: A source is not permitted to wait until READY is asserted before asserting VALID. When VALID is asserted, it must remain asserted until the handshake occurs.

evidence.spec_section: A3.2.2 Channel handshake signals / Table A3-1
evidence.quote: Transaction channel handshake pairs: AW (AWVALID,AWREADY), W (WVALID,WREADY), B (BVALID,BREADY), AR (ARVALID,ARREADY), R (RVALID,RREADY).

evidence.spec_section: A3.3.1 AXI3 write transaction dependencies / Figure A3-6
evidence.quote: The slave must wait for both WVALID and WREADY to be asserted before asserting BVALID. The slave must also wait for WLAST to be asserted before asserting BVALID.

evidence.spec_section: A3.3.1 AXI4 and AXI5 write transaction dependencies / Figure A3-7
evidence.quote: The slave must wait for AWVALID, AWREADY, WVALID, and WREADY to be asserted before asserting BVALID.

evidence.spec_section: A3.3.1 Read transaction dependencies / Figure A3-5
evidence.quote: The slave must wait for both ARVALID and ARREADY to be asserted before it asserts RVALID to indicate that valid data is available.
The earliest point after reset that a master is permitted to begin driving ARVALID, AWVALID, or WVALID HIGH is at a rising ACLK edge after ARESETn is HIGH.
The interleaving of write data with different IDs was permitted in AXI3, but is deprecated in AXI4 and later.
